hero.h1_alt: The supplements worth your money. Nothing else.
hero.subhead: Wellness & Care is a curated marketplace for weight-loss and energy supplements. We select what clinical research supports — and skip everything else. Real results, $100–$300, no hype.

image.alt: Adults aged 25 to 70 in warm natural light, active and energized
image.direction: Real people, authentic, diverse across the 25–70 range. Warm lighting, warm skin-tone saturation against the blue+teal palette. No stock clichés, no gym-bro imagery, no scale-and-tape-measure shots.

problem.h2: You've already spent the money. That's the frustrating part.
problem.body: Diet after diet. Another bottle that promised everything and delivered nothing. The supplement aisle is built to sell, not to work — and there is no easy way to tell the difference from the label.

points.title: Marketing outranks evidence
points.body: The loudest product is rarely the one with research behind it.

points.title: Trial-and-error is expensive
points.body: Every wrong bottle costs you a month and $60–$120 you don't get back.

points.title: Energy is the real cost
points.body: This isn't only about the scale. It's the tiredness that follows you into every day.

how_it_works.h2: Three filters. Everything else gets cut.
how_it_works.lede: We're a curation layer, not a manufacturer. Our only job is deciding what makes the shortlist.

steps.title: Evidence first
steps.body: A product only makes the list if its key ingredients have published clinical research behind them at the dose actually used. Proprietary-blend hiding is an automatic no.

steps.title: Transparency check
steps.body: Full ingredient disclosure, clear dosing, and a real returns policy. If we can't tell you what's in it and what it does, we won't list it.

steps.title: Price sanity
steps.body: Effective doesn't have to mean $500. Our shortlist sits in the $100–$300 range because that's where evidence and affordability actually overlap.

how_it_works.footnote: We earn an affiliate commission when you buy through our links. That commission never influences what makes the shortlist — see our disclosure below.

science.h2: What research supports — and what it doesn't.
science.lede: We'd rather lose a sale than overstate a study. Here's how we read the evidence.

claims.text: Certain ingredients have clinical support for appetite regulation and energy metabolism at specific doses.
Supplements work alongside nutrition and movement — they are a lever, not a replacement.
No supplement treats, diagnoses, or cures any medical condition. Anyone telling you otherwise is selling, not informing.
No product produces the same result for everyone. Individual results vary — always.

science.callout: If you are pregnant, nursing, managing a medical condition, or taking prescription medication, talk to your doctor before starting any supplement.
science.TBD: Client to supply 3–6 citations (study title, journal, year, URL) if the site is to name specific ingredients. Do not fabricate citations.

proof.lede: Every story below is a real customer, published with permission. Individual results vary.
proof.TBD: Client must supply: (a) 3–6 testimonials with name, city, and consent on file; (b) before/after photos with signed written release; (c) any stat used in the stat band. Ship the section with placeholder-free real content or hide the section entirely — never render invented proof.

guarantee.body: Every product on our shortlist carries a 30-day money-back window through the merchant. If it isn't working for you, you send it back. That policy is one of our three filters — a product without it doesn't make the list.
guarantee.fine_print: Refunds are processed by the merchant selling the product, under their published returns policy. Wellness & Care does not process payments or refunds directly. Check the merchant's terms before purchasing.

faq.h2: Questions worth asking before you buy.

items.a: We earn an affiliate commission when you purchase through a link on this site. It costs you nothing extra. Commission rates play no part in what makes our shortlist — evidence, transparency, and price do.

The ingredients on our shortlist have published clinical research behind them at the doses used. That's a meaningful bar, and it's not the same as a promise. Supplements support nutrition and movement; they don't replace them, and results vary between people.

No. The products we list are dietary supplements, not prescription medications. They are not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease. If you're considering a prescription weight-loss medication, that's a conversation for your doctor.
Products on our shortlist sit in the $100–$300 range. We deliberately exclude the $500+ tier — in our reading of the evidence, the extra spend doesn't buy extra efficacy.
The merchants we link to ship across the United States and Canada. Shipping times and costs are set by each merchant.
Yes — every product we list carries a 30-day money-back window through the merchant. Refunds go through the merchant, not through us.

items.q: Should I check with my doctor first?
items.a: Yes, especially if you're pregnant, nursing, managing a health condition, or taking prescription medication. We're a curation service, not a medical provider.

items.q: How often does the shortlist change?
items.a: When the evidence changes. We review the list quarterly and remove anything that no longer clears the three filters.
